key_insight: LLMSurvival makes censoring-aware survival prediction feasible with unmodified LLMs by turning time-to-event learning into pairwise comparisons between comparable patients.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help hospitals use compact LLMs for risk prediction from tabular clinical data while preserving compatibility with censored outcomes.
method: Reformulates survival analysis as pairwise ranking among comparable subjects.
Uses unmodified LLMs fine-tuned on tabular clinical data.
Estimates test-time risk by aggregating comparisons against anchor patients from the training cohort.
evidence_signal: In two clinical tasks (ICU mortality in MIMIC-IV and fragility fracture in a NYP/WCM cohort), LLMSurvival improved concordance over Cox models and several deep learning survival baselines.
watch_item: Results are promising but depend on cohort-specific comparison anchors and external validation is still needed before broad clinical deployment.
paper_title: Towards end-to-end LLM-based censoring-aware survival analysis
